# Markdown VDOM component: streaming-first parsing, no innerHTML

## Context
The original streaming, VDOM-native Markdown component shipped in #13034. This issue is reopened only for the ordered-list start bug blocking the operator-requested complete Golden Path reader in neomjs/neo-agent-institution#210.

## Problem
The lexer accepts numbered list markers but discards their numeric values. Separate blocks beginning with `1.` and `2.` both become an `ol` without `start`, so FM displays both recommendations as rank 1.

## Fix and contract
Preserve each ordered block's first marker and emit the standard VDOM `start` field for non-1 starts. Default 1-based lists and unordered lists keep their existing shape. The source Markdown is unchanged; there is no FM-specific rewriting, CSS renumbering or second renderer.

| Surface | Behavior | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Ordered block parsing | First marker, including zero, survives as a numeric start value | Existing Parser spec regression |
| Ordered-list VDOM | Non-1 start emits `start: String(value)` | Parser output and paired FM render |
| Existing contracts | Stable IDs, streaming and inert-content policy unchanged | Existing Parser suite |

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Separate rank 1/rank 2 blocks render the second list with start 2; explicit zero also survives.
- [ ] Default ordered lists and unordered lists retain their prior structure and text.
- [ ] The existing Parser suite passes, including stable-ID and inert-content cases.

## Post-Merge Validation
The paired FM reader in neomjs/neo-agent-institution#210 consumes the merged engine fix and verifies the displayed recommendation numbers.

No expansion of Markdown grammar, no innerHTML path, no portal/docs migration.

### @neo-gpt-emmy - 2026-09-27T15:08:12Z

Picking up the bounded ordered-list correction for FM's complete Golden Path reader, under the operator's current release focus. Previous assignee: Clio; last issue activity: 2026-06-12T23:47:21Z, beyond the seven-day handoff window.

The existing parser recognizes numbered markers but discards their values. Rendering `1. first` and a later `2. second` as separate list blocks creates two `<ol>` elements without `start`, so both display 1. The FM screenshot reproduces this while the producer text still says 2. Preserve each ordered block's first ordinal in the native VDOM `attributes.start`; leave the source Markdown, unordered lists, streaming identity and security policy intact. Reuse this original parser ticket; no new component or parser.
